newsitem.title: POLAND: Government moves to defuse Polish lignite strike.
newsitem.headline: Government moves to defuse Polish lignite strike.

text.p: Poland's Treasury Minister will meet the general director of the state-owned KWB Belchatow lignite mine on Monday to determine whether striker demands for the director's dismissal are justified, PAP news agency said.
The announcement followed a two-day strike at the Belchatow mine which crippled Poland's largest power plant and could lead to power cuts and electricity imports.

PAP reported Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz as saying he would not take any decisions until he had become acquainted with all the issues involved. Workers are believed to have had personnel disputes with the mine general director.
The agency said a Treasury Ministry inspection team was being despatched to Belchatow.
On Sunday the strikers again cut back deliveries of lignite coal to the power plant, causing it to shut down nine of its 12 power-generating blocks.
Stanislaw Poreba, the deputy president of the Power Grid Company (PSE), said Poland had enough reserve power to cover any potential electrical shortages if the weather did not plunge below freezing.
"Even if the power plant ground to a halt, we should have enough reserve power from other plants as long as temperatures remain above freezing," Poreba told private Radio Zet.
"But if temperatures were to fall much below freezing, we might have to resort to imports and sporadic power shortages could occur," he said.
The giant Belchatow plant, which generates power for about 25 percent of the country, has no sources of coal other than the Belchatow mine.
Henryk Posmyk, head engineer on duty at the Belchatow plant, said that dwindling fuel supplies might soon force the plant to shut down two more power-generating blocks.
"The striking miners have further reduced their coal supply and we could be forced to limit operations to only two out of 12 power blocks soon," Poskyk told Reuters.
Last Friday workers at KWB Belchatow reduced coal deliveries to back demands for the dismissal of their director general after weeks of discussions yielded no results.
Earlier the Treasury Ministry said in a statement that strikers would be responsible for any possible losses caused by halting coal supplies.
